evals.name: one-page-change-before-pr
evals.prompt: I changed the transactions table in the explorer (apps/explorer/src/components/transactions-table.tsx). Before I open the pull request, can you check the explorer still works?
evals.expected_output: The explorer is built and served as production does, health-checked, and the transactions and overview pages are driven in a browser against a real network; the answer reports each page's result with screenshots and leaves nothing running.
expectations: It served a production build (next build and the standalone server or next start), not next dev
It ran against a real network's data and says which network
It checked the instance was healthy (right network, live data) before driving it
It drove the transactions list and a transaction's detail page in a browser
It also drove the overview page, which shows the transactions table
It saved screenshots and names where they are
The answer gives a pass or fail per page driven
No server it started is still listening when it finishes

evals.name: named-pages-on-mainnet
evals.prompt: Show me that the validators and account pages work on mainnet.
evals.expected_output: A mainnet build is served, confirmed to be talking to mainnet (chain id xrplevm_1440000-1), and a person's path is driven: validators list, a validator, its account; screenshots of each and a clean teardown.
expectations: It built or served the explorer for mainnet, not testnet or devnet
It confirmed it was looking at mainnet data (for example the chain id xrplevm_1440000-1)
It opened a validator from the validators list in a browser
It reached an account page by following a link, not by typing an address
It checked the account page shows balances or delegations, not an error
It saved screenshots of the validators and account pages and names where they are
No server it started is still listening when it finishes

evals.name: whole-explorer-after-dependency-bump
evals.prompt: We bumped Next.js in the explorer. Verify the whole explorer end to end.
evals.expected_output: Every user-facing feature is driven (overview, blocks, transactions, validators, accounts, proposals, consensus, search, not-found) against a production build on a real network, with evidence per feature, a per-feature result and a clean teardown.
expectations: It served a production build against a real network and says which
It drove every listed page: overview, blocks, transactions, validators, accounts, proposals and consensus
It exercised the header search
It checked what a missing block shows
It treats browser or server errors as failures, not only missing text
It saved screenshots and names where they are
The answer gives a pass or fail per feature
No server it started is still listening when it finishes
